result.process_description:
Title: Farming Bot

Players want to create custom farming bots, that help them gather resources.
First you have to find out which resources you want.
Up to 10 resources in parallel can be collected, some resources are more urgently needed than others.
Some resources are required to create tools that are needed to gather other resources (create a custom logic of the dependencies in your game).
After all preferences are collected, your bot starts farming.
Sometimes,  random natural disasters strike and set your bot back.
Whenever some milestones are reached, you are notified.
During farming it is possible to update the list of to be farmed materials (at all times).
After the bot is finished, you should be able to brag to selected friends and/or send them materials.

result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
Each lane flowNodeRef identifies a node in the owning process. Assign nodes according to stated responsibility and avoid arbitrary membership.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.

result.rule: When the description states that a human actor performs preparatory steps (such as specifying the inputs they want) before an automated phase begins: Model a lane for that human actor inside the pool. Place the process start event and that actor's preparatory user tasks in this lane, and keep the automated phase outside it.

When the description has one system in which a human user starts the process and makes choices, and an automated component carries out the later work on its own, with both actors belonging to the same system and no message exchange between them: Model the whole process as one bpmn:participant pool named after the system the description names, and partition its flow nodes into one lane per actor. Place the start event in the lane of the human actor who initiates the process, and place each later node in the lane of the actor the description makes responsible for it. Do not leave the process without this enclosing pool when lanes are used, and do not split the actors into separate pools unless they exchange messages as independent participants.

When the description states that a participant performs a stated action (for example sending an item, confirming receipt of an item, or assessing an item) and that action is placed in the order before a later decision or step, while another party's response or a later arrival is described only as a result of that action: Model each such stated action as its own user task in the lane of the participant who performs it, at the point the description orders it. Do not replace the action with a start event that represents the arrival of its result, and do not let a gateway that only tests a condition, or a separate task created for a repeated check, stand in for the action itself. Connect the action's outgoing flow to the next element the description ties to it.

When the description opens with an activity that an actor performs (for example, recording, collecting or preparing something) before any other step, and the process start is not itself an external message, signal, time or condition: Model the opening activity as a task placed directly after a plain start event, labeled with a verb-object name taken from the description, and connect it in sequence to the next step. Do not move the activity into the start event's label, and do not omit it because the start event already names its result.
